sections.title: Welcome and overview
sections.brief: Greet the listener, state what the talk covers, and give the abstract-level one-sentence version of the paper's findings.

sections.title: The feasibility question
sections.brief: Motivation: why quantum-finance claims rest on asymptotics, why the honest question is empirical, and how feasibility can be settled without hardware by measuring scaling exponents, baselines, cost ratios, and precision needs.

sections.title: Primer: how quantum computing works
sections.brief: From-scratch primer: bits vs qubits, superposition, amplitudes, measurement, interference as the true source of speedups, and the overhead of fault tolerance / error correction.

sections.title: Primer: QUBOs, rugged landscapes, and the classical baselines
sections.brief: Define QUBO, local minima and rugged/spin-glass landscapes; explain the two classical baselines: certified Gurobi via exact eigenvalue-shift convexification, and simulated annealing with time-to-solution at 99 percent.

sections.title: Methodology and data
sections.brief: Pre-registration and forking paths, adversarial controls, honesty clauses, zero QPU seconds; the Kenneth French dataset, the two universes, 126-day windows, and the four headline calm/crisis windows.

sections.title: Case study one: QAOA and portfolio selection
sections.brief: The portfolio-selection QUBO, how QAOA works, the fixed-angle protocol and angle concentration, the crisis-hardness hypothesis and its reversal with all headline numbers, the controls, self-averaging, the concentration-hardness trade-off, scaling exponents, the FF100 extension, transfer-gate failure, and the frozen verdict.

sections.title: Case study two: amplitude estimation for tail risk

sections.title: The big picture and conclusions
sections.brief: The three cross-cutting screens (structural hardness, per-operation cost ratio, scale overlap), the self-averaging structural conclusion, and why the negative verdicts do not preclude practical quantum value.
